text:
Nathan MacKinnon is out for at least a month, coach Jared Bednar confirmed after he was hurt in Ottawa on Nov. 12, the same night Cale Makar went down for about two weeks. As the Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal noted, it's MacKinnon's first longer injury since 2022-23, and it lands on the reigning Rocket Richard winner in the middle of another huge start: 30 points in 20 games, 10 goals and 20 assists.

What Colorado loses is mostly the playmaker. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 13.8 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 99th percentile among forwards, and our closest stylistic match is Nikita Kucherov. His scoring this year is honest: 10 goals on 7.94 expected goals (the quality of his chances), a little hot but nothing alarming, and his last ten games produced 14 points against 13 expected. He also still tops the league in our NHL Edge skating-speed data. The question now is how the Avalanche's chances hold up while he and Makar are both gone, and what his rhythm looks like when he returns.
